name: Loktak Lake
description: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for floating phumdis (heterogeneous biomass islands). Ramsar wetland supporting unique ecosystem, fishing communities, and the floating Keibul Lamjao National Park. Located primarily in Bishnupur district near Moirang.
facts: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India (~287 km²)
Ramsar site since 1990
Famous for floating phumdis of vegetation and soil
Supports unique fishing and floating hut communities
About 48 km south of Imphal

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
description: World's only floating national park, located on the southern part of Loktak Lake on a large phumdi. Last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer or dancing deer). Accessed by boat; watchtowers for wildlife viewing.
facts: World's only floating national park
Home to endangered Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii)
Declared national park in 1977 (sanctuary 1966)
Area about 40 km² on floating phumdi
Best visited October–March for birdlife and deer sightings

name: Bishnupur Vishnu Temple
description: 15th-century conical temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu in Bishnupur town, after which the district is named. Built during the reign of King Kyamba; features unique architecture influenced by Chinese styles and local Meitei traditions.
facts: Built in 1467 during King Kyamba's reign
Namesake of Bishnupur town and district
Conical design with Chinese architectural influences
Located in Bishnupur HQ, about 27 km from Imphal

name: INA Memorial Complex (Moirang)
description: Historic site in Moirang where the Indian National Army first hoisted the tricolour on Indian soil on 14 April 1944 under Col. Shaukat Malik. Complex includes museum with INA artefacts, library, auditorium, and statue of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
facts: Site of first INA tricolour hoisting on Indian soil (14 April 1944)
About 45 km south of Imphal near Loktak Lake
Museum displays letters, photographs, uniforms and memorabilia
Administered by Manipur government; key freedom struggle site

name: Loukoipat Ecological Park
description: Small scenic lake and eco-park on the outskirts of Bishnupur HQ, nestled between green hillocks. Offers boating, picnic areas, and panoramic views of the valley; popular local recreation spot.
facts: Located about 1 km from Bishnupur district HQ
Small natural lake surrounded by hillocks
Boating facilities available
Inspection bungalow on adjacent hillock

name: Sendra Island / Tourist Home
description: Rocky hillock island in the middle of Loktak Lake connected by causeway, offering panoramic 360° views of floating phumdis and the lake. Features Sendra Tourist Home and cafeteria; major viewpoint and boat departure point for Keibul Lamjao.
facts: Hillock rising from Loktak Lake
Best panoramic views of phumdis
Sendra Tourist Home managed by Manipur Tourism
About 48 km from Imphal; boat access to national park

name: Moirang
description: Historic town in Bishnupur district near Loktak Lake, gateway to the lake and Keibul Lamjao. Known for ancient Ibudhou Thangjing Temple, Lai Haraoba festival, Khamba-Thoibi epic origins, and INA headquarters during WWII.
facts: About 45 km south of Imphal
Site of INA flag hoisting in 1944
Home to ancient Thangjing Temple
Cultural centre for Meitei folklore and festivals

name: Phubala
description: Charming resort area on the western fringes of Loktak Lake, about 40 km south of Imphal. Offers lake views, boating, and quieter access to phumdis and fishing communities.
facts: About 40 km from Imphal on western side of Loktak
Resort and boat access point
Quieter alternative to main Sendra circuit

name: Red Hill (Lokpaching)
description: Hillock about 16–17 km south of Imphal on Tiddim Road (NH-150) in Bishnupur area. Site of fierce WWII battle between British and Japanese forces; features India Peace Memorial for Japanese soldiers.
facts: About 16–17 km from Imphal on NH-150
Site of WWII Battle of Red Hill
India Peace Memorial for Japanese war dead
Pilgrimage site for Japanese visitors

name: Thanga Island
description: Inhabited island community on Loktak Lake, home to traditional fishing families living on stilts or phumdis. Offers authentic insight into lake life, athaphum fish traps, and Meitei culture; accessible by boat from Sendra.
facts: Traditional fishing village on Loktak
Accessible by boat (~30–40 min from Sendra)
Uses unique athaphum fish traps
Stilt and floating hut dwellings
